DOB: [Date of Birth] (Age: 48)

Diagnosis: Malignant neoplasm of thyroid gland (ICD-10: C73)
Service: IV infusion of selpercatinib (Retevmo) - CPT 96365

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing on behalf of my patient, [Patient Name], a 48-year-old patient under my oncology care, to formally appeal the recent denial of coverage for the IV infusion of selpercatinib (Retevmo), billed under CPT 96365. Please accept this letter and the enclosed medical records as a formal appeal submitted prior to the 30-day appeal deadline. 

According to your denial notice, coverage was denied per the UnitedHealthcare Commercial Medical Drug Policy: Oncology Medication Clinical Coverage. The letter stated that the submitted molecular profile did not document a RET mutation or RET fusion status by an FDA-approved companion diagnostic assay, which is required for approval. 

I am requesting that this denial be overturned immediately because this targeted treatment is medically necessary. The initial prior authorization request inadvertently omitted the complete molecular pathology addendum. I have now attached the patient’s comprehensive molecular profile results, which were obtained using an FDA-approved companion diagnostic assay. As you will see in the enclosed report, the patient’s advanced malignant neoplasm of the thyroid gland (ICD-10: C73) is definitively RET fusion-positive. 

Because the patient has advanced, RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer, the administration of selpercatinib is strictly aligned with the UnitedHealthcare Commercial Medical Drug Policy: Oncology Medication Clinical Coverage. Furthermore, it is directly supported by the NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Thyroid Carcinoma and the NCCN Biomarkers Compendium. Selpercatinib is a highly effective, standard-of-care targeted therapy for RET-altered thyroid malignancies. It is clinically imperative to utilize this specific targeted therapy to halt disease progression, manage the patient's oncological burden, and preserve their quality of life. Withholding this treatment would be detrimental to the patient’s health and survival.

With the inclusion of the attached FDA-approved companion diagnostic assay confirming the RET fusion status, all clinical criteria for coverage have been unequivocally met. I respectfully request that UnitedHealthcare overturn the original denial and promptly authorize coverage for the IV infusion of selpercatinib (CPT 96365) so that we may initiate this medically necessary treatment without further delay.

Thank you for your time, review, and prompt attention to this urgent clinical matter. 

Sincerely,

[Physician Name], MD
[Practice Name]
[NPI Number]
[Phone Number]
[Fax Number]
